key_terms.الرِّئَاسَة: Leadership or headship, specifically the desire for position and authority

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual danger of seeking leadership in Islam according to hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Rida (peace be upon him) employs the vivid metaphor of two predatory wolves among a scattered flock to illustrate the severe spiritual danger of seeking leadership (*al-ri'asah*). He asserts that the corruption of leadership in the religion of Islam is more harmful than these wolves are to the sheep, highlighting how the desire for status can lead to the devouring of communal unity and religious integrity. This teaching is central to Shia political theology, distinguishing between divinely appointed authority and the often corrupting pursuit of worldly power.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Moammar Bin Khallad, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup>.
A man was mentioned and he (the narrator) said, ‘He loves the leadership’.
So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Two fierce wolves among the sheep separated from their shepherd are not more harmful than the leadership is in the Religion of the Muslim’.
en.sarwar: 1. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from Mu’ammar ibn Khallad from abu al-Hassan (a.s.) who has said the following: “It was mentioned before the Imam that a certain man
loves to have leadership. The Imam said, ‘Two fierce wolves in a flock of sheep, whose shepherd is far away, are not more harmful to the flock than seeking leadership to a Muslim’s religion is.’”
